book.title: Things That Must Not Be Forgotten: A Childhood in Wartime China
book.summary: "Son of a wealthy Chinese railway administrator and his Swiss second wife, who soon left him, young David was brought up first by servants and then by an English stepmother in a Eurasian world of privilege, the Legation Quarter of Beijing. The Japanese invasion at first barely touched his family's charmed lives. But as the Japanese overran China, their world began to disintegrate.". "China under Japanese occupation was a changed society fraught with secrecy and peril. David was sent away to school where he was taunted as a half-caste by the now openly anti-Western Chinese. His father served the pro-Japanese government while active in the Resistance. At their summer villa in Beidalhe, the family surreptitiously aided the guerillas in the nearby mountains. And in Qingdao, young David was befriended by the Japanese next door while his father hid a wounded U.S. airman in their house.".
